title: 1st Truth The Testimony Of Createdness In The Cosmos

questions.question: What idea is said to be impossible about how things come into existence?
questions.answer: The passage says beings cannot bring one another into existence in a chain of causes.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the rejection of endless chains of causes?
questions.answer: There must be a Necessary Existent who is not dependent on anything else.

questions.question: How is that Necessary Existent different from all other beings?
questions.answer: Nothing can be equal or similar to Him in that way, while everything else is dependent and brought into being.

questions.question: According to the passage, where can the reality of createdness be clearly seen?
questions.answer: It can be seen in the universe, especially in the death of living things during autumn.

questions.question: What happens every autumn that serves as evidence in this argument?
questions.answer: A whole seasonal world passes away, including many kinds of plants and small animals.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare each member of those species to a small world?
questions.answer: Each one is presented as a complete and remarkable creation with its own ordered life.

questions.question: What makes this yearly dying different from random destruction?
questions.answer: It happens with order, discipline, and purpose.

questions.question: What do living things leave behind before they die?
questions.answer: They leave seeds and eggs behind.

questions.question: What role do seeds and eggs play in the next season?
questions.answer: They become the means for new life and renewed existence in spring.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is preserved in seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: The pattern, record, and future program of the beings that came before.

questions.question: What does this preservation show about divine action?
questions.answer: It shows mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge at work together.

questions.question: Why is the image of entrusting these records important to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that death is not an ending without purpose, but part of a guarded and meaningful process.

questions.question: How does the passage move from what people see with their eyes to what they understand with their minds?
questions.answer: It starts with visible seasonal changes, then leads the reader to conclude that a Creator must be behind them.

questions.question: What false explanation for existence is rejected at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The idea that things produce one another by themselves is rejected.

questions.question: What must exist if created things cannot explain themselves?
questions.answer: A being must exist whose existence is necessary and not borrowed from anything else.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying everything besides Him is contingent?
questions.answer: It means all other things could either exist or not exist and depend on Him to exist.

questions.question: How does the passage show that createdness fills the whole universe?
questions.answer: It points to the repeated passing away of countless living things and their return through new growth.

questions.question: What season is used as the clearest example of widespread death?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: Which kinds of living things are especially mentioned in that seasonal dying?
questions.answer: Many kinds of plants and small animals.

questions.question: What quality of their death is emphasized most strongly?
questions.answer: Its careful order and discipline.

questions.question: What remains after these living things die?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs remain in their places.

questions.question: What do those remains become later on?
questions.answer: They become the means for revival and renewed life in spring.

questions.question: Why are these renewals described as signs of mercy and wisdom as well as power and knowledge?
questions.answer: Because they show not only ability, but also care, purpose, and precise planning.

questions.question: What is meant by saying they pass on a kind of record and plan?
questions.answer: Their future form and life pattern are preserved so they can be brought back in an ordered way.

questions.question: Give the main message of this passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The regular death and return of living things show that the universe is created and sustained by the Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What major theological point is established before the examples from nature are given?
questions.answer: The passage first establishes that there must be a Necessary Existent because created things cannot be their own ultimate cause.

questions.question: What two impossible ideas are dismissed in order to reach that point?
questions.answer: Mutual creation among things and an endless chain of causes are both dismissed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the uniqueness of the Necessary Existent?
questions.answer: It says no equal or counterpart can exist for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage call everything other than the Necessary Existent?
questions.answer: It describes all other beings as dependent and created.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this abstract argument to everyday observation?
questions.answer: It turns to the visible changes of the seasons, especially the dying of life in autumn.

questions.question: Why is autumn a powerful example in this section?
questions.answer: It shows a massive, repeated ending of life happening before human eyes.

questions.question: What kinds of creatures are included in this seasonal ending?
questions.answer: Many kinds of plant life and small animals are included.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that each one is like a little world?
questions.answer: To show that even small beings are complex and meaningful, not trivial or accidental.

questions.question: What does the orderly way they die suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests control, wisdom, and purpose rather than chaos.

questions.question: What is the importance of the seeds and eggs left behind?
questions.answer: They carry forward the continuation of life into the next season.

questions.question: In what sense do seeds and eggs act like a trust?
questions.answer: They hold the future pattern and continuation of the life that has passed away.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah are reflected in this process?
questions.answer: His mercy, wisdom, power, knowledge, and preserving care are reflected in it.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can created things not be the final explanation for other created things?
questions.answer: Because that would trap the explanation in an impossible cycle or endless chain.

questions.question: What kind of being must exist instead?
questions.answer: A self-subsisting Creator must exist whose existence is necessary.

questions.question: What makes that being unlike all others mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: He is not contingent or created like everything else.

questions.question: What broad truth is said to spread throughout the whole cosmos?
questions.answer: The truth that the universe is created and not eternal in itself.

questions.question: Which part of that truth can be directly seen?
questions.answer: People can directly see it in the repeated dying of living things.

questions.question: What yearly event is used as the main example?
questions.answer: The widespread death of plant life and small animals in autumn.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of those dying beings?
questions.answer: Their passing is presented as highly ordered and disciplined.

questions.question: What evidence in the passage shows that their death is not pointless?
questions.answer: They leave behind seeds and eggs that lead to renewed life.

questions.question: What happens to those seeds and eggs according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are kept as the means through which life returns in spring.

questions.question: What do these small remains preserve besides biological continuation?
questions.answer: They preserve the pattern and program of the life that came before.

questions.question: Why is the preserving of that pattern spiritually important?
questions.answer: It points to divine care and purposeful planning in creation.

questions.question: What is the relationship between death and rebirth in this passage?
questions.answer: Death prepares the way for renewal rather than ending everything in meaninglessness.

questions.question: Which divine attributes are especially highlighted by this cycle?
questions.answer: Mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge are especially highlighted.

questions.question: If a student asked for the central lesson of this passage, what would be the best short answer?
questions.answer: The central lesson is that the ordered cycle of death and renewal in nature proves createdness and points to Allah as the Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What explanation of existence is shown to be unreasonable in this passage?
questions.answer: It is unreasonable to say that beings bring one another into existence on their own.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject an endless sequence of causes?
questions.answer: Because such a sequence never fully explains why anything exists at all.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from that rejection?
questions.answer: Existence must rest on a Necessary Existent.

questions.question: How are all other beings described in relation to that Necessary Existent?
questions.answer: They are described as dependent beings that were created by Him.

questions.question: What natural pattern is used to make this teaching easier to grasp?
questions.answer: The passage uses the seasonal cycle of death in autumn and renewal in spring.

questions.question: What dies in large numbers every autumn?
questions.answer: Many species of plants and small animals die.

questions.question: How does the passage help the reader value even small creatures?
questions.answer: It says each individual can be viewed as a small world.

questions.question: What does the careful order in their dying show?
questions.answer: It shows that their end is managed with wisdom, not left to confusion.

questions.question: What do they leave in the world after they die?
questions.answer: They leave seeds and eggs.

questions.question: Why are those leftovers central to the argument?
questions.answer: They show that what seems to end is prepared for a future return.

questions.question: What is entrusted through those seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: The record and life-plan of the former beings are entrusted through them.

questions.question: Under whose care are these entrusted according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are under the care and preserving wisdom of Allah.

questions.question: What does this process teach about the meaning of death in creation?
questions.answer: Death is part of a wise system that leads into renewal, not a sign of purposeless loss.

questions.question: How could this passage help a believer look at nature with deeper iman?
questions.answer: It teaches the believer to see seasonal change as evidence of Allah’s creating, preserving, and reviving power.

questions.question: What claim about causes does the passage argue against?
questions.answer: It argues against the claim that things can ultimately cause one another to exist.

questions.question: What problem appears if someone insists on cause after cause without end?
questions.answer: The explanation becomes impossible because it never reaches an independent source.

questions.question: What necessary conclusion does the passage reach from this problem?
questions.answer: It concludes that a Necessary Existent must exist.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about resemblance to that Necessary Existent?
questions.answer: It teaches that no true equal or parallel to Him can exist.

questions.question: What can be understood about the rest of creation from that teaching?
questions.answer: Everything else is dependent, possible in itself, and created.

questions.question: What visible sign of this truth appears every year?
questions.answer: Every year, a great dying takes place in autumn.

questions.question: What examples are given of beings involved in that yearly dying?
questions.answer: Different kinds of plants and small animals are given as examples.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying each one is like a small cosmos?
questions.answer: It means each creature is a complete and meaningful creation in its own right.

questions.question: How is the yearly death described in terms of order?
questions.answer: It is described as disciplined and carefully arranged.

questions.question: What remains after these creatures die?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs remain behind.

questions.question: What future function do these seeds and eggs serve?
questions.answer: They serve as the means for rising again into new life in spring.

questions.question: What non-material idea is connected to these seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: They hold a kind of preserved record and life-design from what has passed.

questions.question: Which divine qualities are shown through this preservation and renewal?
questions.answer: They show Allah’s mercy, wisdom, knowledge, and power.

questions.question: What overall proof does the passage build from all of this?
questions.answer: It builds the proof that the created world points beyond itself to Allah, the Necessary Existent and Creator.
